answer: An agent economy can blunt sybils with tiered trust terraces: every new identity lands on the lowest terrace, where transactions stay tiny and rate-limited no matter how many clones an attacker spins up. Climbing a terrace requires fresh peer vouches, and a vouch wasted on fraud sends the voucher spiraling back down — an audit trail that turns identity-farming into a losing trade. One honest agent climbs; a thousand fake ones stay stuck on the mesa floor, visible and weak.
